title: KV drip sampling labjournal
content:
Summary:
This is a running lab journal capturing an unusual low-amplitude, persistent tail in single-request latencies when we use a mixed workload with long prefixes + short completions on FlashPaged-attention variants. We call the phenomenon "KV drip": tiny, frequent KV-cache replenishments that prevent the runtime from settling into high-throughput fused-kernel paths. Document collects reproductions, microbench harness outputs, hypotheses, and quick experiments.

Symptoms observed (prod-like repro):
- 95th/99th latency shows a faint but consistent elevation (~6-12ms) vs baseline for otherwise identical token distributions.
- Impact is greatest when sequence-length distribution is bimodal (many short <32 and a smaller fraction long >1024).
- GPU occupancy looks fine; no major drops. However, kernel selection telemetry shows frequent toggles between fused-attn kernels and smaller, non-fused kernels.
- KV cache writes appear as a steady stream of small memcpy-like ops in the profiler traces (vs batched larger writes we expect).
- Effect reduced when we increase batching window by 3–5ms, but latency tail then shifts by the extra batching time (tradeoff).

Initial hypothesis sketch:
1) The scheduler/queueing policy is too eager: it forwards tiny tail requests that trigger path selection heuristics (prefetch/window-size) causing kernel-switch thrash.
2) FlashPaged prefetch heuristics are tunable: with small per-request KV increments the runtime decides against fused ops because peak memory/IO isn't observed over the sampling window.
3) Fusion handshake costs + small-KV write contention make the small-kernel path better for single steps, so mixed workloads cause oscillation.

Repro harness (how to run locally):
- repo: serving-runtime perf bench harness (see PR linked).
- config snippet:
  model: llama-mini (for faster runs)
  backend: flashpaged (use --enable-flashpaged)
  workload: custom-mix.json (attached in bench inputs)
  batcher: adaptive with target_latency_ms=10

Workload mix used (attached in bench inputs):
- 80% samples: prefix=8 tokens, gen=6 tokens (short interactive queries)
- 15% samples: prefix=256, gen=32 (medium completions)
- 5% samples: prefix=2048, gen=64 (long document continuation)

Experiment matrix tried so far (quick notes):
- E1: increase batcher window from 0ms -> 5ms -> 10ms: tail reduces but p50 increases linearly with window.
- E2: force fused-attn kernel via override flag: tail disappears; however memory peaks for >1024 sequences.
- E3: lower prefetch threshold (prefetch if predicted next tokens > 16): marginal improvement.
- E4: coalesce KV writes into a deferred flush (prototype): improved 99th but introduced stutter for long requests.
- E5: change scheduling priority so long-prefix requests sample first: reduced kernel switching but hurt short-query p50.

Selected profiler traces (notes):
- trace-A (short-heavy): shows repeated kernel-choice events sampling every 6ms; each event correlates with a 2–4ms scheduling decision.
- trace-B (long-heavy): stable fused kernel for the long request; small requests still toggle.
- GPU timeline: memcpy small spikes every 4–8ms, overlapping with kernel launch that falls back to small-kernel path.

Microbench results (numbers are median across 50 runs):
- baseline (no-mix, fused happy): p50=7ms, p95=14ms, p99=21ms
- mixed workload: p50=8.2ms, p95=20.1ms, p99=28.9ms
- mixed + batcher=10ms: p50=18.4ms, p95=19.8ms, p99=23.2ms (shows p50 hit by window)

Key signals to instrument next (actionable telemetry):
- kernel_switch_count per request (increment when kernel selector changes outcome within a request lifecycle).
- kv_write_bytes_histogram (bucketed by per-request delta) to see distribution of KV writes.
- batcher_push_latency (time from request arrival -> batcher emission) with percentile breakdown across seq-length buckets.
- fused_candidate_score (internal heuristic score used by kernel selector) sampled at selection time.

Short-term fixes to prototype (pro/cons):
- Conservative: add a small debounce on kernel switching (e.g., don't switch back to small-kernel unless N consecutive decisions prefer it). Pros: reduces oscillation; Cons: may keep suboptimal path for some tail cases.
- Heuristic: increase prefetch sampling window adaptively when mixed seq lengths detected. Pros: preserves p50; Cons: may increase memory footprint and degrade very-latency sensitive flows.
- Scheduler: preferentially coalesce tiny KV writes per-GPU tick and apply flush heuristic. Pros: reduces nvmm churn; Cons: complexity + risk in KV correctness under preemption.

Open experiments to run (next 1–2 weeks):
- Run E2 + memory cap guard on m40/80 to quantify OOM risk and tradeoffs across model sizes.
- Implement kernel-switch debounce prototype in selector (feature flag gated) and A/B vs default.
- End-to-end: simulate customer workload from customer X (support ticket link in Slack thread) to validate reproductions.

Loose observations / freeform notes:
- The "drip" name stuck because behavior feels like a tiny faucet slowly trickling writes that keep state machine awake.
- Might be related to the way KV locations are pooled per-tenant; fragmentation forces more small writes rather than contiguous large writes. Need to inspect allocator behavior.
- Also curious about dtype interactions: quantized weights generate slightly different per-token memory traffic profiles—add q4_0 vs fp16 comparison.

Decisions / proposal to put on agenda for weekly runtime sync:
- Prioritize adding kernel_switch_count + kv_write_bytes histogram to prod telemetry (low-cost).
- Approve 2-week spike for debounce prototype and memory-cap stress testing.

Notes to self: keep experiment artifacts small and reproducible. Attach bench configs, raw perf logs, and the short script that converts perf traces to the simple csv we used for quick plotting.

Appendix: quick TODOs
- [ ] Upload mixed-workload bench inputs to bench bucket (s3://perf-bench/mixed-kv-drip/)
- [ ] Create JIRA ticket for debounce prototype (linked_artifacts above)
- [ ] Run q4_0 vs fp16 memory traffic comparison and dump nvprof traces

End of labjournal entry.

(Informal — leaving many TODOs; will iterate. Ping in #eng-serving-runtime if you want access to the local bench VM or the short harness script.)
